title: Apply A House Style To Word Documents Without Collateral Damage
taskName: Apply A House Style To Word Documents Without Collateral Damage
summary: Word documents from a review pipeline carry tracked changes, comments and their anchors, footnotes, a content control, a custom XML part, bookmarks, a hyperlink, an embedded image, numbered lists, headers and footers. The agent must apply four named house-style changes and leave everything else exactly as it was. This targets a real and silent failure: a tool that models paragraphs and runs but not revisions or content controls rewrites the document on save and drops what it does not understand, producing a file that still opens and looks right while having lost the review history. Grading is exhaustive: package parts the brief does not name must be byte-identical, and the body must be unchanged once alignment is normalised away.
agentMustDo: Inspect the sample documents under `input/documents` and find what they contain beyond paragraphs.
Justify every body paragraph except Heading1 and Heading2, which are left-aligned, including paragraphs inside tables.
Change the Heading1 colour in word/styles.xml to 7A2E2E.
Replace the [[CYCLE]] placeholder in both the header and the footer with 'Q1 2026'.
Leave every other package part byte-identical, and leave every revision, comment anchor, footnote reference, bookmark, field, drawing and content control in place.
Write output/restyle.py, invoked as `python3 restyle.py <input.docx> <output.docx>`, that works on unseen documents of the same shape.
evaluation: evaluate() runs the submitted script over seven held-out documents. For each, the edit half checks all four named changes and the preservation half checks that unnamed package parts are byte-identical and that the document body is unchanged once w:jc is normalised away. reward = 0.7 * (documents where both hold) + 0.15 * (preserved) + 0.15 * (edited). Reference outputs are produced by running the reference edit, not hand-authored. Grading is deterministic and offline; no judge model or credential is required. Measured against deliberate failure modes: dropping tracked changes, the content control, comment anchors, a footnote reference, the custom XML part or the comments part each score 0.150, while harmless variations such as pretty-printing an edited part or re-ordering the zip score 1.000.
